## TL;DR

This slice closes the review loop around repeat findings and remaining non-blocking risk. Reviewer output now requests one complete enumeration of each bug class, while the parser treats the required grepping closer as report structure rather than a bug. Completed review passes retain finding classes for convergence history. After the configured freeze, a human can create a follow-up task from suggestions; in Move to done, a human can record a reason for accepting a `needs some work` verdict only when that verdict is the sole failing landing check. The review drawer reports the current round and configured freeze. Round 1 review also caught a reviewer prompt that had accidentally received engineer-only handoff language; that text is removed and covered by a regression assertion.

## Work and rationale

The reviewer mission in `src/server/review.ts` already describes whole-class enumeration and emits the exact “No further findings…” closer. The accidental final self-review sentence was aimed at the engineer and appeared in the reviewer report template, even though the engineer’s `DEFAULT_AGENTS` prompt already owns that handoff checklist. I removed only the misplaced sentence. The reviewer role prompt in `src/core/config.ts` now explicitly says not to stop at the first instance, matching the acceptance wording. Prompt tests assert both that the reviewer sees this enumeration direction and that the engineer handoff instruction does not leak into the mission.

The review report parser and pass history support stable class labels, which the UI renders in the task drawer. The review history shot fixture previously showed two pass rows while leaving the task’s round count at zero. It now seeds two completed rounds, class labels on both rows, and a freeze count of four. The round guidance reads `freezeAfterPasses` from review state and falls back to four when older or unavailable server responses omit it. This keeps the estimate meaningful when a project changes the setting. I added a focused highlight class to the hint and declared a task shot for the review drawer so the capture points at the new guidance rather than the unrelated header badge.

The route integration test drives a real test server. It confirms that follow-up creation is rejected before the four-pass freeze even when suggestions exist, and that Land anyway rejects a report containing blocking Bugs. The production route still requires a current `needs some work` review, a non-empty reason, and every non-verdict landing check to pass. The override records the human reason in task activity and then continues through the existing close-out pipeline; it does not skip checks.

The broader feature also adds CLI parity for follow-up creation, persisted round and finding-class history, the Move-to-done confirmation flow, and workflow documentation. No new setting was introduced; the existing freeze setting remains user-adjustable through Settings. The design keeps follow-up creation explicitly human-triggered and records accepted risk at the task level.

## Approaches tried

I first removed only the misplaced sentence and added a regression test in the existing default-prompt suite. Review feedback also identified that the prompt’s equivalent “WHOLE CLASS” wording did not satisfy the acceptance criterion’s literal instruction, so I added the explicit “Do not stop at the first instance” sentence rather than relying on implication. For the round hint, I replaced the hard-coded estimate with the setting returned by the review endpoint and kept the existing default for compatibility.

For route coverage, I used the repository’s real-server integration test harness instead of testing a detached predicate. The new fixture produces a `needs some work` report containing both a concrete blocking finding and a suggestion; the test then exercises the follow-up and done HTTP endpoints and checks their rejection reasons.

## Challenges and blockers

The first integration-test attempt called Move to done while the fixture task was still active, so it correctly received a task-state validation response before reaching Land anyway eligibility. I revised the test to submit a real review request, wait for the report and handoff slot to settle, and only then call the endpoints. The scoped feature-specific tests pass after that correction.

An earlier handoff check also exposed a jsdom teardown race in overlay inspection: a MutationObserver callback could execute after the global `Element` binding was removed. The existing fix uses `nodeType` before casting and has a regression test that removes the global while the callback runs. A prior remote check separately timed out in the unrelated orphaned-lock test; a full local check passed at that time. This task does not change the housekeeping failures tracked by #1076 or #1061, as requested.

## Key learnings

Prompt ownership is a correctness boundary: shared review output templates should not absorb engineer workflow rules, even when the underlying checklist is useful. Literal acceptance language also matters when reviewers or tests audit prompt behavior. UI fixtures should seed all state that is visible together—history rows, round count, finding classes, and configured freeze—so captures communicate a coherent state. Finally, route tests need to wait for the whole review handoff lifecycle, not just the presence of a report, because the done endpoint correctly refuses to race an active automatic review.
